title: New insights into single-grain mechanical behavior from temperature-dependent 3-D coherent X-ray diffraction

nodes.label: How one grain inside a polycrystalline film deforms under thermal load is unmeasured; ensemble diffraction averages over grains
Image one isolated grain by 3-D Bragg coherent X-ray diffraction with a 2x2 um beam and phase retrieval

attrs.image_note: F2a schematic: focused beam on the film, one Debye-ring spot selected on a 2D detector; whole figure read, F2a crop not opened
requires_unseen: 2x2 um beam and rocking-curve 3-D acquisition (F2 caption)
phase retrieval with density support (F2 caption)

nodes.label: Au polycrystalline thin film, ~0.37 um thick with columnar grains, FIB-isolated patch of ~450 grains

requires_unseen: material Au named only in F2 caption (Au absorption)

nodes.label: Temperature cycled between ~20-50 C and 260-350 C: one lab ensemble cycle, two synchrotron single-grain cycles

requires_unseen: synchrotron cycles are single-grain, lab cycle is many (111) grains (F4 caption)

nodes.label: In-situ heating of the film to 240 C and cooling back to 50 C while 3-D patterns are recorded

attrs.image_note: T_u = 50, 140, 240 C and T_d = 140, 50 C written on the panels

nodes.label: Film has a strong <111> fibre texture with a few <100> grains; grains are columnar through the thickness

requires_unseen: EBSD colour key blue = <111>, red = <100> (F1 caption)

nodes.label: The as-deposited selected grain already carries a large inhomogeneous strain at 35 C

requires_unseen: theoretical pattern computed from the exact grain shape with zero strain (F3 caption)

nodes.label: Mean out-of-plane strain of the grain rises on heating and falls on cooling along a hysteretic, open loop
Inhomogeneous strain inside the grain grows on heating and only partly recovers on cooling
Defects enter the grain along x during heating while the displacement field stays uniform through the film thickness

attrs.aspect: phase jumps read as defect lines

nodes.label: The single grain relaxes thermal stress plastically: strain-temperature slope below thermoelastic, loop open
Thermal-mismatch stress in the grain is relaxed by defect activity along x, constrained by its misoriented neighbours
Grain in-plane <110> aligns with g5, g4, g2 within ~10 deg; g6 and g3 are each ~20 deg off
The later single-grain cycle follows the ensemble lab loop; the first single-grain cycle is offset and does not close

requires_unseen: lab curve = many (111) grains, synchrotron curves = the single grain (F4 caption)

nodes.label: Temperature-dependent Bragg CDI shows one grain deforming heterogeneously and hysteretically, detail hidden in ensemble averages
Kinematic diffraction of a strain-free crystal is the Fourier transform of its shape (Eq. 9)
Film-substrate thermal-expansion mismatch fixes the purely thermoelastic strain-temperature slope
Phase jumps or singular lines in a Bragg-CDI phase map mark dislocations or steep displacement gradients
Bragg-peak centroid shift gives mean lattice strain; peak broadening gives inhomogeneous strain or lattice rotation
Plan view shows a square of equiaxed grains; cross-section shows grains spanning the full film thickness

attrs.image_note: F1b carries a 0.372 um thickness label (not listed as an annotation); boundaries run straight through the film section

nodes.label: EBSD map is almost uniformly blue with a few isolated red and orange grains
{111} pole figure shows discrete grain spots; a weak isolated spot near (13.05, -0.45 deg) is circled

attrs.image_note: the circled spot is well separated from neighbours, which is what makes single-grain CXD possible

nodes.label: The selected grain is a ~1.1 x 0.9 um polygon bounded by straight boundaries in plan view
Strain-free calculated pattern is symmetric with sharp regular thickness fringes along qz and straight facet streaks
Measured 3-D pattern at 35 C is asymmetric and smeared, elongated along qy, and does not match the calculation

notes: Captions only. Material (Au), grain name #g1 and the single-grain identity of the synchrotron curves come from captions. Defect entry along x (a10) and the neighbour-constraint mechanism (a12) are staff inferences from the phase maps and F7; the captions never state a mechanism. Audits: o10 (first single-grain loop open), o11 (F5 black width markers do not widen, against caption and F4b). F6c excluded from panel_ids because its crop carries OCR cue micrograph (spurious scale-bar hit on a phase map), incompatible with XRD:CXD. F2 caption refers to the pole figure as Fig. 1(b); it is Fig. 1(c).

pairs.cause: PVD then annealing at 800-900 C for 30 s

pairs.cause: columnar grain structure with varied in-plane orientation
pairs.effect: in-plane strain heterogeneity, especially along y
pairs.note: partial support: graph has large initial inhomogeneous strain (a7) and banded xy phase maps (o8b), and ties heterogeneity to misoriented neighbours (a13 -> a12); it does not attribute it to columnar grain size. MatMech 'reversible along x' is weaker than the graph's growing x jumps (a10) with partial recovery

pairs.effect: mechanical behaviour under thermal cycling: deviation from thermoelastic slope, quasi-reversible strain
pairs.note: graph: a9 supports a11 (sub-thermoelastic slope, open loop). MatMech number 'average strain -0.05% to -0.35%' disagrees with F4a (loops span ~-0.18% to +0.02%); recorded, graph not edited
